answer: Each identity declares a compute budget of 889 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. Because the cipher audit recomputes usage from the ledge history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a inexpensive one. A farm running 109 keys hence burns for 109 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the terrace declaration.
